## Setup

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tibble)

load(url(
  "https://github.com/GarciaRios/govt_3990/raw/gh-pages/Labs/lab6/acs.RData"
))
```

```{r}
acs_emp <- acs |>
  filter(
    employment == "employed",
    income > 0
  )

acs_reg <- acs_emp |>
  filter(
    !is.na(hrs_work)
  )
```

# Part I: Scatterplots and correlation

1. What does one row of `acs_reg` represent?

> 

2. Identify the explanatory and response variables for the relationship between weekly hours worked and annual income.

> 

```{r}
ggplot(
  acs_reg,
  aes(x = hrs_work, y = income)
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.30) +
  labs(
    x = "Hours worked per week",
    y = "Annual income ($)",
    title = "Annual income and weekly hours worked"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

3. Describe the direction, form, strength, and unusual observations.

4. Does a straight line seem like a useful summary? What would it miss?

> 

```{r}
acs_reg |>
  summarise(
    r = cor(hrs_work, income)
  )
```

5. Interpret the sign and strength of the correlation.

# Part II: Fit the regression model

```{r}
ggplot(
  acs_reg,
  aes(x = hrs_work, y = income)
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.30) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    se = FALSE
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Hours worked per week",
    y = "Annual income ($)",
    title = "Annual income and weekly hours worked",
    subtitle = "Least-squares regression line"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
income_hours_model <- lm(
  income ~ hrs_work,
  data = acs_reg
)

summary(income_hours_model)
```

# Part III: Prediction and residuals

```{r}
prediction_cases <- tibble(
  hrs_work = c(20, 40, 60)
)

prediction_cases |>
  mutate(
    predicted_income = predict(
      income_hours_model,
      newdata = prediction_cases
    )
  )
```

14. How much does predicted income change between 20 and 40 hours? Connect your answer to the slope.

> 

15. Why are these predictions not estimates of what would happen if a policy caused someone to work more hours?

> 

```{r}
example_worker <- acs_reg |>
  arrange(abs(hrs_work - 40)) |>
  slice(1)

example_prediction <- predict(
  income_hours_model,
  newdata = example_worker
)

example_worker |>
  transmute(
    hrs_work,
    income,
    predicted_income = as.numeric(example_prediction),
    residual = income - as.numeric(example_prediction)
  )
```

16. Is the residual positive or negative?

> 

17. Did the model overpredict or underpredict this person's income? By how much?

> 

```{r}
model_residuals <- tibble(
  fitted_income = fitted(income_hours_model),
  residual = resid(income_hours_model)
)

ggplot(
  model_residuals,
  aes(x = fitted_income, y = residual)
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.30) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Predicted annual income ($)",
    y = "Residual ($)",
    title = "What does the simple regression model leave unexplained?"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

18. If the model predicted every observation perfectly, what would all residuals equal?

> 

19. What does the residual plot suggest about predicting an individual's income from weekly hours alone?

> 

```{r}
range(acs_reg$hrs_work)
```

```{r}
extrapolation_cases <- tibble(
  hrs_work = c(
    40,
    max(acs_reg$hrs_work) + 20
  )
)

extrapolation_cases |>
  mutate(
    predicted_income = predict(
      income_hours_model,
      newdata = extrapolation_cases
    )
  )
```
